summary:
Parallax is a mobile decision tool that helps mission designers and researchers find Earth locations that best simulate the Moon or Mars environment for training and equipment testing.

We collected and cleaned environmental data for 187 analog sites worldwide, standardizing measurements across temperature, atmosphere, radiation, moisture, and terrain. A weighted similarity algorithm compares each site against planetary reference conditions and ranks them by environmental match.

What makes Parallax different is mission-driven filtering: instead of a fixed ranking, users set their own priorities — blocking sites with weaknesses in conditions that matter most to their mission — without altering the original scientific scores. The app adds a warning system that flags exactly where each site underperforms, a full detail page comparing every measured value against the target planet, and a side-by-side shortlist comparison of up to three candidate sites.

The result is a tool that turns hours of manual research into a decision made in seconds — built for the analog mission planning community that currently does this work by hand.

Beyond research institutions and universities, Parallax targets space agencies and private space companies as a viable commercial opportunity. The platform can evolve into a SaaS model offering licensed access to mission planning teams, with potential API integration for organizations conducting large-scale analog site assessments.
details:
Parallax is a mobile decision tool that helps mission designers and researchers identify Earth analog sites — locations whose environmental conditions resemble the Moon or Mars — for training, equipment testing, and mission simulation.

How it works: We collected environmental data for 187 analog sites from USGS, NASA POWER API, Open-Elevation, and NASA Fact Sheets, covering 10 attributes across temperature, atmosphere, radiation, moisture, and terrain. A weighted similarity algorithm compares each site against Moon and Mars reference vectors and ranks them by environmental match with 98.5% consistency across sensitivity analysis scenarios.

What makes it different: Instead of a fixed ranking, users set their own mission priorities — filtering out sites with weaknesses in conditions that matter most to them — without altering the original scientific scores. The app adds a warning system flagging where each site underperforms, full detail pages comparing every measured value against the target planet, and side-by-side shortlist comparison of up to three candidate sites, ending with a one-tap generated mission brief ready to share.

Tools & Stack: Flutter & Dart for cross-platform mobile development, BLoC pattern for state management, go_router for navigation, dartz for functional error handling, and shared_preferences for local persistence. Data processing was done in Python.

Creative approach: Most analog site research lives in scattered academic PDFs. Parallax turns that into an interactive, filterable, mission-aware tool — one that respects the science by never reinventing the score, only helping the user navigate it. The result is a research-grade decision tool with a consumer-grade experience.

Intended impact: Parallax targets the analog mission planning community — research centers, universities, and space agencies currently doing this work manually — with a path toward a SaaS model serving institutional and commercial space organizations.

Key factors our team considered: Scientific transparency — never modifying the original scores; data reliability — sourcing exclusively from NASA and USGS; and usability — ensuring a researcher could reach a decision in under a minute without reading a single paper.
